Amazon RDS's db.x2g classes are powered by AWS Graviton2 processors, by RDS's page on its instance class types, and a Graviton processor runs one hardware thread, one vCPU, per physical core, by the AWS Graviton performance runbook (https://aws.github.io/graviton/perfrunbook/system-load-and-compute-headroom.html). EC2 sells no x2g types, so its specification tables do not list the family.
T2 instances run one thread per core, on Intel processors: AWS's specifications of the general purpose instances give every T2 type as many CPU cores as vCPUs, at one thread per core.
AWS's page for M7a says that every vCPU of an M7a instance is a physical core, with no simultaneous multithreading; on M6a and earlier a vCPU is a thread.
AWS's page for C7a says that every vCPU of a C7a instance is a physical core, with no simultaneous multithreading; on C6a and earlier a vCPU is a thread.
AWS's page for R7a says that every vCPU of an R7a instance is a physical core, with no simultaneous multithreading; on R6a and earlier a vCPU is a thread.
